# 09 — OpenMausBot: features, architecture, and what Jaari borrows

Studied 2026-11-10 from `refs/openmausbot` (https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot,
Apache-2.0 except `enterprise/`, commit `b802268`; pin in `refs/INDEX.md`). Paths below
are relative to that repo. Claims were read in code unless marked *docs only*. Decision
taken: ADR-016 (accepted). Open questions added: OQ-51 to OQ-56.

## 1. What OpenMausBot does

**Product.** A chat app in which every contact is an agent ("bot") with its own
instructions, model, computer, and connected apps. Bots run on the CLIs the person
already has (`claude`, `codex`, `grok`, and 24 more drivers), so work is billed to an
existing subscription. Desktop app (Electron), phone companions, a headless CLI, an MCP
server, and a server mode for a VPS.

**Features.**

| Area | What it has |
|---|---|
| Agents | 27 drivers behind one SPI (`server/contracts.ts`, `server/drivers/builtIn.ts`): Claude stream-JSON, Codex JSON-RPC, a shared ACP core, Pi over `pi --mode rpc` (`server/drivers/pi.ts`), OpenAI-compatible endpoints; custom engines by config |
| Computers | Cloud desktop (Boat, third party), local container VM pinned by image digest, the person's own machine through cua-driver, a VPS over SSH; a bubblewrap sandbox around engine processes on Cloud (`server/bot-box/`) |
| Browser | Own CDP driver or agent-browser, per-bot profiles, saved logins filled without the bot seeing them, owner hold, a SOCKS5 egress gate (`server/browser/egress/`) |
| Approvals | Five levels mapped onto each engine's native modes; inline Allow/Deny cards; exact-command and MCP-read standing grants; an optional shell safety floor |
| Memory | Per-bot Markdown workspace (`MEMORY.md`, topic files, archive, daily logs), background capture, nightly tidy, an undo journal, a shared "About me" |
| Proactivity | Routines (once, daily, interval, cron), webhooks on a separate listener, app events through a hosted queue, a daily brief built without a model |
| Connectors | Composio sessions, custom MCP servers, skills as `SKILL.md` plus manifest |
| Coordination | One assignment tree for bot-to-bot work, room goal runs, a small "decision model" that routes messages |
| Sharing | Team, department, and preset files with secret scrubbing; import from other products |
| Voice | Spoken replies, half-duplex calls, spoken approvals |
| Remote | Noise-encrypted phone link with a QR-pinned key, a relay that sees no content, HPKE for secrets typed on the phone |

**Architecture.** Two processes. A harness server on loopback owns every agent process
and exposes HTTP commands plus one SSE stream; the app holds no transports. Each driver
normalises its provider's protocol into one canonical event union
(`shared/runtime-events.ts`); a raw tee of the native protocol is kept beside it so
drift shows up in a diff (`server/drivers/native.ts`). Messages live in SQLite; durable
job state is a second SQLite database with an append-only events table and ten
invariants that can rebuild a row's status from its events (`server/runtime/store.ts`,
`server/runtime/invariants.ts`). The per-thread NDJSON event log is for inspection and
is lossy on purpose (`server/harness/bus.ts`). The host file `server/index.ts` is about
15,600 lines.

## 2. Why it does it that way

| Failure prevented | Mechanism | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Policy changed between approval and send | Re-read policy, scopes, and capability just before dispatch; refuse with "the outbound policy changed" | `server/outbound-hold.ts` (`beforeDispatch`) |
| A standing grant outlives the thing it was granted for | MCP read grants keyed on a SHA-256 of the server config; an edit revokes | `server/provider-tool-allow.ts` |
| A half-parsed command auto-approved | The shell lexer returns "unreadable" when it cannot read to the end; unreadable becomes a card | `server/safety-floor.ts` |
| Injected text steering later work | Outside origin is sticky across everything a job spawns; confined jobs reach an allowlist of routes; their memory writes need a card with the full text | `server/host/outside-lineage.ts`, `server/host/outside-fence.ts`, `server/read-and-draft.ts` |
| DNS rebinding, redirects to private hosts, WebRTC leaks | Gate resolves, checks every address, dials only those; one address-class table with NAT64 and 6to4 unwrapping; loopback bypass removed; own ports denied | `server/browser/egress/gate.ts`, `server/browser/egress/policy.ts`, `electron/egress-addresses.mjs` |
| Datacenter IP rejected by the person's own accounts | Only a short list of "home sites" leaves through the person's lent computer, which re-checks each connection; the rest goes direct (all-home was 1.7 to 30 times slower) | `server/browser/egress/home-sites.ts`, `electron/device-egress.mjs` |
| Agent and owner typing at once; owner's typing seen by the model | Hold owned by the person: drain accepted calls, refuse (never queue) bot input, grace and idle timers | `server/browser/session-control.ts`, `server/browser/hold.ts`, `server/computer-control.ts` |
| Password in model context | `fill_login` types the saved value; evaluation and screenshots are refused until the field is cleared; held values scrubbed by exact value and encodings | `server/login-fill.ts`, `server/browser/cdp/secrets.ts`, `server/secret-vault.ts`, `shared/redact.ts` |
| Model invents a path or URL to read a credential | The bot names a fixed target id; "the id is the entire authority surface" | `shared/credential-request.ts` |
| A crashed turn sends twice | A cut turn reruns at most once, never if an outward action was seen; replay decided from protocol state (before or after accept) | `docs/runtime-contract.md` §5, `server/resume-recovery.ts` |
| Fallback to a model that cannot do the job | Backup refused unless it has the original's tools and workspace; policy reads capability flags, not driver names | `server/automatic-recovery.ts`, `server/runtime/capabilities.ts` |
| Invented facts about the person in memory | Capture must quote the person; code checks the quote exists and that numbers, paths, and URLs come from it | `server/memory-capture.ts` (`statedInConversation`), `server/memory-fact-checks.ts` |
| The bot rewriting its own memory history | Journal stored outside the bot's writable area, with actor, hashes, and diff per change | `server/memory-journal.ts` |
| A forgotten fact relearned next week | Removed facts remembered by identity; forget-words blocklisted | `server/profile-learned.ts` |
| Routines that burn tokens to say "nothing new" | Plain-code checks first; model runs only on new ids; "NOTHING NEW" posts nothing; cursor moves after the result is kept; 24 model runs a day | `server/host/routine-checks.ts`, `server/routine-check-pacing.ts`, `server/automation-reports.ts` |
| Slow routine builds a queue; laptop slept through a run | Anchor-aligned intervals, overlap skip or queue, one catch-up within 12 hours, otherwise a missed-run receipt | `shared/routines.ts`, `server/routine-intervals.ts` |
| Webhook endpoint exposes the app | Separate loopback listener, secret stored hashed and compared in constant time, auth before body, 256 KB cap, rate limit, delivery-id dedup, payload fenced as untrusted | `server/webhooks.ts` |
| Bot adds a tool server, then swaps its address | Approval card bound to a SHA-256 of the target; nothing applied if it changed | `server/routes/internal-mcp.ts`, `server/host/mcp-requests.ts` |
| Mumbled "okay" taken as consent | Spoken answer must open the utterance and be an unconditional yes or no | `shared/call-consent.ts` |
| Tampered native binary | Per-platform SHA-256 and size, SBOM, no runtime self-update | `third_party/cua-driver/`, `server/browser-engine-release.ts` |
| Sandbox silently weakened by a refactor | Boot self-check plus mutation tests that remove one protection at a time | `server/bot-box/self-check.ts` |
| Evals that measure the model, not the product | Hermetic scripted engine, JSON scenarios, pure scorers, redacted golden threads | `evals/README.md` |
| Prompt cache thrown away each turn | Stable and volatile prompt parts; tool list pinned byte-for-byte by a test; keep-warm with a cost guard | `server/drivers/prompt-split.ts`, `server/cache-keepwarm.ts` |

## 3. What Jaari does, and where it differs

**Borrowed (ADR-016, accepted).** Re-check at dispatch; "unreadable is not clear";
hash-chained `audit.jsonl` with rule, actor, presence, and medium (the chain is from
`connector/src/audit.ts`, the row fields from `server/decision-log.ts`); the restart
rule; resolve-check-dial egress with one address table; exact-value secret scrubbing,
typed credential targets, and no screenshots over a filled secret; owner-hold semantics.
None of these changes a package boundary. They specify behaviour that `@jaari/gate`,
`@jaari/http`, `@jaari/secrets`, and `@jaari/computer` were going to need anyway.

**Borrowed as leanings on open questions.** Pairing with a QR-pinned key and hashed
device tokens (OQ-02, OQ-37); FTS-only recall with a fixed budget, placed before the
owner's message (OQ-03, OQ-04); the events-table job store (OQ-05); struck-through
superseded facts and a forgotten-fact list (OQ-09); stall guard (OQ-11); canonical event
union plus raw tee (OQ-12); notification QA rules (OQ-13); config-fingerprinted MCP
grants (OQ-14); sandbox self-check (OQ-15); spoken-consent grammar (OQ-16); harness
evals (OQ-20); the home-sites split (OQ-32); routine semantics (OQ-43); byte-stable tool
list (OQ-44); pinned sidecars and capability flags (OQ-50).

**Where Jaari is already stronger, and stays as it is.**
- Approval binding. OpenMausBot binds an approval to a random request id on a suspended
  request and shows arguments cut at 400 characters (`server/outbound-requests.ts`).
  Jaari binds to a SHA-256 of the whole action, which survives a restart and cannot be
  replayed (ADR-006).
- Defaults. Its default level is Full access (`shared/approval-mode.ts`,
  `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_MODE = "full"`), and "Approve for me" hands the decision to the
  provider's LLM reviewer. Jaari has no LLM in the approval path (principle 9) and
  starts in shadow mode (OQ-47).
- Outbound detection. It recognises sends by verbs in tool names (`shared/outbound.ts`).
  Jaari maps every tool to a declared capability.
- Untrusted content. It defuses text with regexes and confines the run; it has no
  tool-less reader. Jaari keeps the reader role and may add its sticky lineage (OQ-54).
- Memory. No git; undo is an NDJSON journal. Upkeep rewrites memory on its own by
  default. Jaari keeps git and reviewable writes (ADR-003, ADR-004) and takes only the
  evidence check and the line conventions.
- Proactivity. No quiet hours, no dials, no ledger across sources; throttles are
  constants. ADR-008 already covers more.
- Egress. One gate per browser session, but the local VM container has no egress
  restriction and there is no single HTTP egress package. Jaari's single path is kept.

**Rejected as a poor fit.** The roster of bots, rooms, Chief of Staff, and team cloud
(a multi-agent product; agent-to-agent is a v1 non-goal); vendor CLIs as the main loop
(ADR-001; a narrow version is OQ-56); the Electron shell that host control depends on;
the hosted relay, hosted Composio broker, and Boat cloud desktop; a decision model that
fails open; the lossy event log as a record.

**Open after this study.** OQ-51 (standing grants), OQ-52 (inbound triggers), OQ-53
(memory capture evidence), OQ-54 (outside lineage), OQ-55 (external control surface),
OQ-56 (subscription CLI engines).

**Numbers worth keeping.** Outbound approval card expires after 9 minutes; a native ask
after 15. Routine catch-up window: 12 hours. Model runs per routine: 24 a day, backoff 15
minutes to 4 hours. Webhook body cap 256 KB, 10 requests a minute. Recall budget: 4 notes
plus 4 passages in 6,000 characters. `MEMORY.md` load cap: 200 lines or 24 KB. Owner hold
release: 2 minutes after the last view closes, 5 minutes idle. Room-routing decider: 1.5 s
timeout, accept at 0.6 or above.
